parts.gloss: he who does not feel ashamed

literal: If oneself does not feel ashamed of that which is fit for others to feel ashamed, virtue possesses that which is fit to feel ashamed of him.
translation: If a person does not feel ashamed of an act that makes onlookers feel ashamed, virtue itself will feel ashamed to remain with him.
modern: பிறர் வெட்கப்படக்கூடிய ஒரு செயலுக்குத் தான் வெட்கப்படாமல் இருந்தால், அறமே அவனைக் கண்டு வெட்கப்பட்டு அவனை விட்டு நீங்கும் தன்மையைக் கொண்டிருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the critical role of a sense of shame in maintaining moral character. When a person commits a wrong deed that makes even others feel embarrassed on their behalf, yet remains shameless, they lose their moral compass. The poet personifies virtue (அறம்) to explain that it will feel ashamed to dwell with such a shameless person and will abandon them. Thus, shamelessness completely drives away all goodness and virtue.
